result.note: Tests Venezuela's place in India's crude supply and reserves, and the Strait of Hormuz closure behind the June 2026 Modi–Rodríguez meeting.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez in New Delhi. Consider the following statements about India–Venezuela energy ties at the time:
items: Venezuela had become India's third-largest oil supplier.
Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves.
Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery is the top buyer of Venezuela's dense crude.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements match the story. Venezuela became India's third-largest supplier, it holds the world's largest proven reserves, and Jamnagar is the top buyer of its dense crude. Venezuelan crude is heavy and high in sulphur, so only a few specialised refineries, such as India's, can process it profitably.
questions.source: India wants crude while Venezuela has the world’s largest proven reserves.

questions.prompt: By June 2026, Venezuela had become India's third-largest oil supplier, filling a gap left by the closure of which waterway?
questions.explain: Venezuelan crude filled the void left by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the turmoil in West Asia. New Delhi is pursuing Venezuelan oil for long-term energy security, across both upstream extraction and downstream refining.
questions.source: She lands in New Delhi as Venezuela becomes India's third-largest oil supplier, filling the void left by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
